subject.title: fix(security): bound skill-file audit read (restore removed fs dependency)

question: Should an oversized or non-regular SKILL.md be reported as a scoped code-safety finding while the rest of `security audit --deep` continues, rather than allowing this read to determine the whole audit outcome?
rationale: The patch changes a security-sensitive file-read boundary, and the intended failure semantics are not demonstrated in the PR evidence.

options.title: Preserve scoped audit completion
options.body: Add a focused regression test and runtime proof showing normal SKILL.md scanning still works and an over-cap or invalid file yields the intended per-skill audit result without stopping other audit work.

options.title: Accept whole-audit failure
options.body: Document and explicitly approve failure of the deep audit when this bounded skill-file read rejects, including the operator-visible error contract.

recommendation.title: Preserve scoped audit completion
recommendation.body: Add a focused regression test and runtime proof showing normal SKILL.md scanning still works and an over-cap or invalid file yields the intended per-skill audit result without stopping other audit work.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged ownership of the SKILL.md audit behavior makes this the closest available routing candidate.
